proof_summary: Lucas congruences split each defining sum for \(p\le n\le2p-2\) into vanishing middle terms and cancelling \(k,k+p\) pairs, while \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\pmod p\) and the vanishing of \(\binom{2k}{k}\) above the midpoint give the two required anti-diagonal values at \(n=p-1\). Thus each Hankel matrix is zero above its anti-diagonal, so only the reversal permutation contributes to its determinant; its sign \((-1)^{p(p-1)/2}=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) combines with the anti-diagonal product to yield the stated residues.
